skill.name: Show a character through action and speech
skill.why: Telling 'she was angry' is flat. Showing it lets readers work it out.
skill.how: Don't name the feeling. Show what the character does and says instead.

beats.say: Telling names the feeling. It's quick, but it's flat.
Showing lets the reader spot the feeling for themselves.
You can show it with an action.
beats.show: Mo **chewed his sleeve and checked the oven nine times**.

beats.say: Or show it with what they say.
beats.show: **'It's fine. It's totally fine. Is it on fire?'**

beats.say: Now we know Mo's nervous, and we never said it.

weDo.frame: Mo is writing about the day Wren met a snake at the park.
weDo.prompt: Which sentence shows that Wren is brave?
weDo.hint: Which one lets you see Wren do something?
weDo.success: Stepping in front of a snake is brave, and her calm words prove it. You worked it out.

options.text: Wren stepped between the snake and the little kids and said, 'Everyone back up. Slowly.'

options.reason: This tells us she's brave. It doesn't show us anything she does.

options.text: Wren was the bravest girl in the whole world.
options.reason: Still telling. A bigger word isn't the same as showing an action.

weDo.frame: Mo is reading out his story about Zed's game night.
weDo.text: Zed threw his controller onto the couch, folded his arms and muttered, 'This game is rigged.'
weDo.hint: Look at what his hands do and what he says.
weDo.success: Throwing the controller and blaming the game both show frustration, without the word ever being used.

options.reason: Excited people don't throw things and mutter. His arms and words show he's fed up.
Someone sleepy wouldn't throw a controller. The action is too sharp and cross.

creature.name: Tawnip
creature.blurb: A frogmouth that never tells you how it feels. Watch its feathers puff and its beak clack, and you'll know.

workshop.mentor: Nan didn't sit down once in the whole first quarter. She stood on her seat with a thermos in one hand and a sausage roll in the other, and every time the umpire blew the whistle she pointed the sausage roll at him like a sword. 'Are you blind, mate? That was holding the ball!' A man in front turned round to complain. Nan gave him one look over her glasses. He turned back very quickly. At three-quarter time, she leaned over and whispered, 'If we lose, nobody tells your grandfather I cried.'
workshop.ask: Show a character without naming the feeling. Ideas: Maxx when his stream crashes, a nervous goalkicker, a kid who broke the TV, a proud cat.
checklist: I showed it through something my character does.
I showed it through something my character says.
A friend could guess the feeling from my writing.
